issues.claim: suggested_pricing fallback: a draft-only tier at USD 450/month is "still under Native Base and above Cert Desk's entry block".
issues.problem: Contradicted by the plan's own cited competitor price. Salience Cert Desk is USD 499/month for the 150-certificate block (verified on the InsurTech List page the plan cites), so a USD 450 tier is BELOW Cert Desk's entry block, not above it. The positioning statement (and the implied 'premium to a cheaper point solution') is therefore wrong by USD 49/month.
issues.fix: Either reword to 'still under Native Base and just under Cert Desk's USD 499 entry block' and drop the premium implication, or set the draft-only tier at USD 520-550/month if the intent is to sit above Cert Desk; keep the comparison labelled inference.

issues.claim: current_tools: service channels are 'Phone (732.521.0001), a still-published fax line (732.521.4945), email and in-person service during Mon-Fri 9am-5pm hours', evidence cited to the contact page.
issues.problem: The contact page I opened shows both office phone numbers, the fax number and Mon-Fri 9am-5pm hours, but no email address (only a contact route). The 'email' channel is not supported by the cited page. Minor, and does not affect any price, rule or integration.
issues.fix: Cite a page that actually publishes a service email address (e.g. an about/claims page) or reword to 'phone, fax, in-person and web form during Mon-Fri 9am-5pm'.

claims_checked.claim: Hetzner Cloud Regular Performance shared cloud from EUR 5.49/month excl. VAT, with US cloud locations in Hillsboro, Oregon and Ashburn, Virginia.
Postmark Pro is USD 16.50/month starting at 10,000 emails/month, extra emails USD 1.30 per 1,000, inbound email processing included on Pro.
Gemini 3.8 Flash paid tier is USD 0.75 per 1M input and USD 3.75 per 1M output tokens through 31 Dec 2026, then USD 1.50/USD 7.50 from 1 Jan 2027.
Gemini's pricing page marks the free tier 'Content used to improve our products: Yes' and the paid tier 'No'.
Claude Haiku 5.5 is USD 0.10 input / USD 0.50 output per MTok for prompts up to 100,000 tokens.
Anthropic documents that US-only inference via inference_geo incurs a 1.1x multiplier on all token pricing categories.
Anthropic's commercial terms state 'Anthropic may not train models on Customer Content from Services'.

AMS360 Web Service API is provided at no additional charge (Vertafore FAQ), with agency-provisioned WSAPI login, pre-defined or custom entity sets, Specific Employee / Employee Supplied by Web Service / Entity Access Security Only scoping, and an SDK needed by whoever writes the program.
Vertafore notes EMS and OData APIs expose additional endpoints not available through Web Services APIs, and the public page does not enumerate which entities exist per WSAPI version.

Applied Epic REST APIs exist at the Applied Dev Center, with credentials generated on the site and a production application requiring name, email, organization name, enterprise ID and Epic database name.

Applied's Service Portal is 'the product formerly known as Applied CSR24', generates certificates from live account coverage on the latest ACORD forms or the agency's own templates, applies account-level reissue rules, attaches a secure link and QR code, and logs every certificate action to the account.
Applied Epic Service Portal / CSR24 price is not public ('no price shown on the product page').
Microsoft Graph exposes Outlook mail resources including message, mailFolder and attachment for read/send/attach operations.

Salience Cert Desk: first 25 certificates free, then USD 499/month for 150 certificates (about USD 3.33 each), a holiday rate for sign-ups by 31 Dec 2026 held for the first 6 months of billing; integrations AMS360, Applied Epic, HawkSoft, NowCerts; commercial property and general liability only.

Native Base: first automation USD 2,499 once, charged only if live and in use by day 14, then USD 2,499/month flat, USD 4,499/month for two build lanes, month to month, no per-certificate charges; works with AMS360 and Applied Epic among six systems.
HawkSoft Self-service Certificates: flat $49 monthly fee per agency, no per-certificate fees.

Certificate Hero advertises realtime AMS integrations, data-driven templates, a live ACORD editor with validation, logged certificate actions, language/endorsement library, insured self-service portal and an Open API; no price is shown on the site.

Certificate Hero's help centre documents an automatic AMS sync every 4 hours plus a manual 'Insured Sync' button, and states it does not ingest endorsements and cannot track which certificates included endorsement forms.

ReSource Pro Certs Center: standard on-demand certificates typically issued within two to four hours, rush requests averaging two hours, production-based pricing (pay per certificate or per renewal account) with no published rates.
New Jersey median annual wage for Insurance Claims and Policy Processing Clerks (SOC 43-9041.00) is USD 59,810, median hourly USD 28.76, 10th percentile hourly USD 22.63 (BLS 2025 data).
Loaded rate of USD 35.95/hour = NJ clerk median hourly USD 28.76 x 1.25 benefits assumption.
Audit sizing arithmetic: 2-4 staff x 1,800 hours x 35% on certificates x 25-45% template-standard = 315-1,134 hours; at USD 35.95/hour that is roughly USD 11,300-40,700.

Per-certificate model arithmetic: 5,000 input + 2,000 output tokens at Gemini 3.8 Flash = USD 0.01125/certificate (about USD 4.50 at 400 certificates) and at Claude Haiku 5.5 = USD 0.0015/certificate (about USD 0.60 at 400); 1.1x US inference on Claude gives about USD 0.66/month.
Running-cost totals: 6 + 16.50 + 5 + 5 = 32.50 low and 20 + 16.50 + 20 + 5 = 61.50 high, i.e. about USD 33-62/month; without Postmark 16 to 45.

Suggested-pricing cash arithmetic: USD 3,500 set-up plus 3 x 750 + 9 x 850 = USD 13,400 in year one; Native Base year one 2,499 + 12 x 2,499 = USD 32,487 (13,400 is about 41% of that); Cert Desk 499 x 12 = USD 5,988; 13,400 is about 22% of USD 59,810 and about 52% of the USD 26,000 midpoint of the benefit range.
Build effort totals about 21 founder-days (2+5+4+5+4+1), consistent with '8-10 weeks part-time, about 4-5 weeks full time'.

N.J.A.C. 11:17A-1.4(b)(13) lists 'authorizing the issuance or delivery of certificates of insurance...' and (b)(14) responding to a policyholder's request for advice or counsel on coverage among selling/soliciting/negotiating activities, which (a) bars without a producer licence.
N.J.A.C. 11:17C-2.5(h) requires a client file kept at least five years after termination of coverage, including 'All correspondence received or sent'.

N.J.A.C. 11:17C-2.6(c)(3) permits electronic recordkeeping only if 'electronic back ups are produced daily and, at least every 30 days, the records maintained electronically are reproduced and stored off-site'.
N.J.A.C. 11:1-44.1(b) states 'This subchapter shall apply to all licensees as defined herein' (state GLBA safeguards subchapter).
DOBI Bulletin No. 25-03, dated 11 Feb 2025, is addressed 'TO: ALL INSURERS AUTHORIZED OR ADMITTED IN NEW JERSEY' and sets insurer expectations including due diligence on third-party AI vendors.

IIABA certificates white paper (second edition, March 2008) reports about 1 in 25 E&O claims involves a certificate, over half arising from CSR error or omission, with failure to add/improperly identifying additional insureds (36%) and misrepresenting coverage (21%) as the two main sources.
PIA states 'ACORD requires all users of ACORD forms, including independent agents, to obtain an ACORD Forms End User License, regardless of how users access the forms.'
Docling, the cantoo-scribe pdf-lib fork and LangGraph each carry an MIT licence on their repository pages.
